Consonantal i

SearchHow we decideRulings

Macrons

Consonantal i

Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

serious adjective

in earnest, not joking; of a person, grave

also seriously, are you serious?, in earnest, earnest, joking aside, seriousness

classical

Cic. Off. 1.134: sī sēriīs, sevēritātem adhibeat, sī jocōsīs, lepōrem
Hor. S. 1.1.27: āmōtō quaerāmus sēria lūdō

sērius, sēria, sērium

adjective; as a noun, sēria, serious matters

serious, earnest (of things said or done)

The opposite of jocōsus: in jest or in earnest, jocō an sēriō. Classical writers use it only of things; of a person they say sevērus (Lewis & Short).

Examples

  • sed tamen āmōtō quaerāmus sēria lūdō

    but still, joking aside, let us look into serious thingsHor. S. 1.1.27

  • Jocōne an sēriō illaec dīcat, nesciō

    whether he says that in jest or in earnest, I don’t knowTer. Heaut. 541

  • Vērōn' sēriō?

    Really? Seriously?Plaut. Merc. 685c

  • lūdō autem et jocō ūtī illō quidem licet, sed sīcut somnō et quiētibus cēterīs tum, cum gravibus sēriīsque rēbus satis fēcerimus

    we may indeed enjoy play and joking, but, like sleep and other rest, only when we have done what serious and weighty matters requireCic. Off. 1.103

Other words

  • sēriō — seriously, in earnest

    adverb · classical · Plaut. Merc. 685c: Vērōn' sēriō?; Ter. Heaut. 541: Jocōne an sēriō illaec dīcat, nesciō; Traupman 107, 376: sēriōne dīcis tū?, are you serious?

    (vōx sermōnis cotīdiānī: Plaut., Ter.; later Liv., Quint.; not in Cicero or Caesar (Lewis & Short))

    A favourite word of Plautus. Vērōn' sēriō?, “Really? Seriously?”

  • sevērus, sevēra, sevērum — serious, grave, stern (of a person or a face)

    adjective · classical · Cic. de Or. 2.228: omnium gravissimus et sevērissimus (Lewis & Short); Cic. de Or. 2.289: vultus sevērior et trīstior (Lewis & Short)

    Also strict and severe: the same word serves for a serious face and a stern father.

  • gravis, grave — serious, dignified, weighty (of a person: the opposite of levis)

    adjective, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Lael. 95: inter … levem cīvem, et inter cōnstantem et vērum et gravem; Traupman 157, 376

    Seriousness is gravitās (Traupman 157).

See also serious, important.

SourcesLewis & Short: serius · Lewis & Short: severus · Lewis & Short: gravis
